description: The approved video stream sent from the Video Management Service to the child could be intercepted or viewed by unauthorized parties during transmission or at the receiving endpoint, revealing the child's viewing choices and potentially sensitive preferences or habits.

description: This flow stores government ID images in the file-system uploads datastore. title: JWT in localStorage can directly identify the user if accessed by scripts or local attackers
description: Storing a JWT in browser localStorage places identity-bearing claims or a stable subject identifier at the destination data store. If JavaScript running in the origin, a malicious extension, or another local attacker can read localStorage, the token may reveal who the user is or enable account takeover that effectively identifies the user behind the browser session.

title: Persistent JWT in localStorage enables cross-session linkability
description: A JWT stored in localStorage can persist across browser restarts and be reused across requests within the same origin. This creates a stable identifier that can link multiple actions, sessions, or visits to the same user or browser context.
assumptions: The token lifetime is non-trivial or the application refreshes it in a way that preserves a stable account-linked identifier.

title: JWT storage in localStorage increases risk of data disclosure
description: localStorage is readable by any script executing in the application's origin, so an XSS flaw or malicious third-party script can exfiltrate the JWT. Because the flow stores the token at the destination data store, disclosure of the token and any embedded claims is a realistic privacy threat.
assumptions: The browser environment may execute injected or third-party scripts, or the endpoint device may be shared or compromised.
uncertainty_note: Node id is best-judgement; the core disclosure threat is strong and well-established for localStorage token storage.

description: Persisting a JWT in localStorage can retain personal data or an account-linked bearer token longer than necessary for the authentication purpose, especially if expiry, revocation handling, or logout cleanup are weak. This may violate privacy requirements around storage limitation, confidentiality-by-design, or minimizing locally stored personal data.
assumptions: The JWT persists beyond the strictly necessary session duration or contains personal data in claims.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on system policy, token contents, and whether localStorage is cleared reliably on logout/expiry.
